blocks.content: The Central Bureau of Investigation serves as the premier investigating agency of India, tasked with upholding integrity in public administration and investigating complex crimes.

rows: Anti-Corruption, Economic Crimes, and Special Offences
Terrorism and Scheduled Offences Impacting National Security
Statutory Body created by the NIA Act, 2008
Requires General or Specific Consent of State Govt (Sec 6, DSPE Act)
Has concurrent jurisdiction nationwide without requiring state consent

items: CBI is NOT a statutory body—it was set up by an executive resolution and draws investigation powers from the DSPE Act, 1946.
Under Section 6 of the DSPE Act, CBI requires the consent (general or specific) of the respective state government to conduct investigations in its territorial jurisdiction.

The CBI Director is appointed by a statutory committee consisting of the Prime Minister (Chairperson), Leader of Opposition/Single Largest Party in Lok Sabha, and the Chief Justice of India (or a nominated Supreme Court Judge).

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) was established in 1963 by an executive resolution of the Ministry of Home Affairs on the recommendation of the Santhanam Committee.
CBI is not a statutory body; it derives its investigative power from the Delhi Special Police Establishment (DSPE) Act, 1946.
It currently functions under the Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions, Government of India.
CBI serves as the official National Central Bureau (NCB) of Interpol in India, facilitating international law enforcement cooperation.
